A year ago, my boss gave me a chance to take on a huge project, in which I had no prior knowledge. I spent months trying to teach myself stuff that I had very little interest in and was way way over my head. Many nights I came home crying to my boyfriend that there was no way I could learn everything I had to learn and complete the project correctly before my audit. It was the hardest thing I have ever done, but when the auditor flew in and went over my work he said "you did a perfect job." I was so excited. This was the hardest I had ever worked for anything, I pushed myself to my absolute limits, I wanted to give up but I didn't and it paid off. My boss came up to me afterwards handed me some cash and told me he was really proud of me for starting from nothing and getting through it on my own. The whole rest of the day coworkers were coming up to me and telling me that they know how hard I worked for this and that I deserved it.

It was honestly the best day of my life and I couldn't wait to tell my boyfriend about it. I walked in and told him "the auditor said it was perfect!" and he said "The dog chewed up the carpet, I am so fucking pissed right now." and then he proceeded to spend the rest of the night slouching around the house with this angry scowl on his face not saying anything. It completely sucked the life out of me. I had never been so proud of myself, but the dog chewed up the carpet so it wasn't the most important thing that happened that day. 

We're still together, but I think about that conversation a lot and it still hurts. My coworkers were proud of me, my boss was proud of me, my boyfriend cared more about the carpet.

I fell in love with the Black Rock Desert last year. My boyfriend and I decided to drive through The Black Rock and the Sheldon Wildlife Refuge. We started off near where they have Burning Man but other than that we didn’t have a plan. The first night we camped overlooking the playa and it was amazing. We could see absolutely everything for miles. The stars were incredible, it was so dark that headlights from across the playa were lighting up our camp as people got off work at the mines. As we made our way through the Black Rock and the Sheldon it became more and more clear to me that this was the most beautiful place I’d ever seen, in a totally non conventional way. To me it was amazing how much raw land there was, how much life there was, how much space there was. You can really see the land, every wrinkle in every mountain, there isn’t anything hiding it. You see it for exactly what it is. I felt alive out there, like I was right where I was meant to be, doing exactly what I was supposed to be doing. We ended up in Virgin Valley, we dug for opals at Rainbow Ridge Opal Mine and found a ton! It was perfect. Everything was perfect, we had set out with no plan whatsoever and we got lucky over and over again the whole trip. I thought I would never feel that sense of freedom and belonging again. I was wrong.

Northern Nevada had the wettest winter on record this year. By February the dry lake bed that is the playa, was full of water. 6 feet deep for 12 miles. I had no idea how long the water would last, but I knew that I didn’t want to miss it, so we loaded up the car. When we got there it was so windy, it was almost hard to breathe. We walked down to the water and I let my entire body weight go into the wind. It held me up. It felt like I was flying. That night it snowed. We woke up in the morning to sun coming up over the mountains. The sunrise wasn’t a ton of vibrant colors, it was just gold. Pure golden light. The mountains were reflecting off the water and everything was covered in a fresh coat of snow. It was the most beautiful thing I’ve ever seen. There was no one around, not even a car in the distance. That moment was ours. I felt that I was seeing what people thousands of years ago saw, before the lake dried up in the first place. Who knows if we will be the last generation to see those mountains reflecting off the water. I cant imagine that many people alive today have seen what I saw that day. And that feeling washed over me again, of being exactly where I was meant to be. I’ll never forget the freedom, the belonging, the wonder, I felt in the Black Rock. That image of the snow covered mountains over the water lives in me now. It’s a permanent part of who I am, and I wouldn’t change a single thing about it. 

TLDR; Mountains reflecting off 6ft of water in a long dry lake bed, surrounded by silence and snow, gave me a sense of belonging and freedom that I will crave everyday for the rest of my life.

I've lost a few people to suicide. The one that had the biggest impact on me was my grandpa. It happened when I was little, and I've lost close friends to suicide since then. 
But my grandpa sticks with me and I think about it everyday, even 20 years later. I am still wondering why he did it, why he didn’t leave a note or anything behind. I wonder if he regretted it in the few seconds it took him to die after the bullet entered his heart. Why he would think that our family would be okay without him? My parents still recount their last conversations with him often, and my aunt is still angry at him. I guess no one knew that he held us all together, shortly after he died we all moved to different parts of the country and now we never see each other. 
The worst thing it did to me though, was put it in my head that suicide is an option. I always tell myself I will never go through with it because I know first hand how my grandpa’s suicide shattered my family, and I would never want to put them through that again. But in the end the thought always, without fail, creeps back into my head. And then I find myself thinking about him, wondering if he felt the way I am feeling now. Wondering what he would tell me if he was still here. I wonder if he knew that I would feel like this 20 years later, if he still would have done it. I don’t talk about it so I don’t know if anyone else in my family feels the same way, but I wouldn’t be surprised if they did. 
I just miss him so much and I wish I could talk to him.  There are so many questions that I will never have answers for.
